source.title: Fix the Loss, Not the Radius: Rethinking the Adversarial Perturbation of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Jin-Ping Wang; Qin-Han Liu; Zhiwu Xie; Zhi-Qiang Gao

record.tranche_reason: Compares training methods on held-out accuracy and measures Hessian-based properties, using different methods from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study compares LE-SAM with SAM and other methods on test accuracy and reports Hessian and LPF measurements. These findings concern generalization and flatness, but do not test the specific conditions or magnitude-aware sharpness measure in the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima generalization premise to develop LE-SAM and evaluates its performance. It tests none of V1–V8: Hessian eigenvalues, trace, LPF, and landscape visualizations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of train–test gaps at comparable training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they argue that fixed-radius SAM has a gradient-norm-dominated surrogate, propose a fixed loss budget to shift the signal toward curvature, and report improved accuracy and flatter solutions. The mechanism explanation is the authors' interpretation, not a demonstrated test of V7.
record.recipe_differences: LE-SAM fixes a loss-space budget and derives a dynamic perturbation radius, rather than using SAM's fixed-radius perturbation.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports sensitivity to the LE-SAM loss budget σ: smaller values weaken perturbation, while overly large values may harm optimization stability; performance is described as relatively stable from 0.3 to 0.5 on CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18.

fits_no_version.finding: LE-SAM has higher reported mean accuracy than SAM across the recorded CIFAR, ImageNet, and ViT fine-tuning comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-equated SAM improves held-out accuracy over fixed-radius SAM in the tested image-classification settings.

fits_no_version.finding: LE-SAM yields lower reported maximum Hessian eigenvalue, Hessian trace, and LPF in the ResNet-18 CIFAR-100 analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LE-SAM produces flatter solutions than the compared methods according to these particular flatness metrics.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper reports three random seeds and uncertainty for several accuracy results, but does not give uncertainty for the Hessian/LPF comparisons in the supplied text. The reported flatness metrics are not directly correlated with train-test gaps among models at comparable training loss. Figure-only metrics have no stated numeric values.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out performance on natural and random labels.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or Adam-to-SGD switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that mitigate large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects across data sizes and configurations, including removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus train–test gaps among comparably fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded accuracy values agree with the supplied tables. Additional method-performance experiments concern LE-SAM+, domain generalization, adversarial robustness, and long-tailed classification; none supplies a missing test of V1–V8. State cannot_determine denotes inability to establish a listed version, not inability to read the accuracy values.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under differing tuning, decay, and switching conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness correlated with train-test gaps among models with similarly low training loss; the study reports Hessian eigenvalues, trace, and LPF instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
